split_mtu_4096_fits_whole.note: a frame that fits is returned unchanged and unwrapped

kiss.note: FEND C0 -> DB DC, FESC DB -> DB DD; leading C0 00 is FEND + command

want_with_depth.note: odd payload length: the trailing byte is remaining depth, and the receiver clamps it to its own default

cancel.note: WANT + CANCEL, never a depth byte, so the length stays even

cancel_all.note: empty payload is the wildcard: retire every interest this peer placed

leaf.name: dam.txt
leaf.note: MANIFEST_TAG, no depth byte: a depth-0 manifest encodes exactly as it did before trees existed

tree.name: big.bin
tree.note: TREE_TAG carries a depth byte; chunk_ids name sub-manifests, not chunks

sealed.note: SEALED_TAG carries depth and a 16-byte hdr_id naming the header envelope; name is empty and total_len is the plaintext length

forwarding.why: the ordinary path: deliver locally and relay on every interface but the one it arrived on

forwarding.input: the same DATA a second time
forwarding.why: dedup is by envelope id with hops zeroed, so one message arriving by two paths is one message
hops counts down and forwarding stops at zero; the frame is still for us, it just stops here

forwarding.state: dest is neither ours nor a topic we follow
forwarding.why: custody: unicast we cannot read is carried anyway, which is what makes the mesh a courier

forwarding.input: INV listing an id we lack
forwarding.why: INV and WANT are per-link, hops=0, consumed on receipt: never stored, never deduped, never relayed

forwarding.input: WANT for an id we hold
forwarding.why: answered on the link it arrived on rather than flooded, because exactly one peer asked

forwarding.input: WANT for an id we lack
forwarding.why: nothing to serve; the node may adopt an interest and ask onward, which is not a reply to this link

forwarding.input: DATA with created_at far in the future
forwarding.why: post-dated frames are refused at admission: one would otherwise outrank every honest envelope at eviction

forwarding.input: DATA whose payload was altered after signing
forwarding.why: relayed and delivered anyway, and that is the rule rather than a gap: SPEC section 5 says verify before binding trust state, do not verify to forward. A relay moves bytes it cannot read. What the bad signature costs the sender is attribution - the envelope binds no path, names no neighbour, and reaches the app flagged for the app to check - so a second implementation that drops it here is not stricter, it is broken, because it would also drop every envelope it merely lacks the key for
